approvalTitle: tasks.md: converting the functional decomposition graph (written against the recommended amendments)
content:
# Tasks Document

One Developer owns this specification, per CLAUDE.md's one-owner-per-specification rule, and works it in one worktree (`.claude/worktrees/fdgd`, branch `features/functional-decomposition-graph-disl-fbl`). **The order is the design's nine steps and it is load-bearing**: the transcript is frozen before anything changes (task 1), the menus are derived before the findings (tasks 6 and 7), the findings before the reading (task 9), and the reading before the writing (task 10), so that a difference in the transcript can be attributed to one change. Design step 3 is three tasks here (3, 4 and 5) and design step 8 is two (10 and 11), because each would otherwise be too large for one pull request.

**Every task is one pull request into `develop` and leaves the four gates green.** A task whose transcript differs in a way this document does not name is not delivered. A path that begins with `backend/` or `client/` is inside `src/diagrams/functional-decomposition-graph/`.

**Task 2 is done in etalii-adp/etalii.adp**, through that repository's own pull request. Tasks 3, 4 and 5 start by loading its definition, and task 5 cannot start before it is merged there.

**Task 3 is shared library work.** The graph functions of DISL 12.4 are also needed by `causal-loop-disl-fbl` and `azure-devops-pipeline-disl-fbl`. Whichever specification reaches its library step first delivers them. If they are on `develop` when task 3 starts, task 3 takes them as given and adds only what is still missing.

**Tasks 9, 10 and 11 wait, and task 12 waits with them.** Reading and writing the body through the binding need two constructs FBL 0.2 does not have: a slot that reads a YAML scalar as written (gap 1) and a constant written by an `insert` (gap 2). Both are a language change in etalii-adp/etalii.adp, which is that repository's own specification. The default of Q5 is whatever is ruled for Q3 of `timeline-disl-fbl`, whose default is to report the gap and wait. **Nobody starts task 9 before FBL has both constructs, or before Q3 of `timeline-disl-fbl` is ruled "work around it".** Until then the tool reads with `FdgParser` and writes with `FdgWriter`, and tasks 1 to 8 are complete without them. Task 12 closes the specification and follows task 10.

**This document is written against the recommended option of each amendment the design proposes; a ruling that differs is a small amendment to the tasks named.** Amendment 1 (the order of findings is held in three places by `FdgFindingOrder`, and finding A13 and gap 8 are reworded) touches tasks 1, 2, 7 and 12. Amendment 2 (the `.fdg` case of `ModuleCrossCheck.Tests` is added while `FdgParser` is product code and moves with it into the module's test project) touches tasks 9 and 10.

---

## The coverage diff, run before this document was raised

**56 acceptance criteria in the requirements; 56 claimed by the tasks below; none unclaimed, nothing claimed that is not a criterion, and none claimed twice.**

| 2 | 6 | 2 (2.1, 2.2, 2.3, 2.4), 5 (2.5, 2.6) |
| 3 | 8 | 6 (3.1, 3.8), 7 (3.2 to 3.7) |
| 4 | 8 | 9 (4.1 to 4.8) |
| 5 | 10 | 10 (5.1, 5.2, 5.3, 5.5, 5.6, 5.7, 5.9, 5.10), 11 (5.4, 5.8) |

| 9 | 4 | 1 (9.4), 12 (9.1, 9.2, 9.3) |
| 10 | 4 | 5 (10.3), 12 (10.1, 10.2, 10.4) |

A criterion that more than one task works towards is claimed by the task that completes it. Criterion 3.1 names the refusals of a connect, which task 7 derives; task 6 claims it because the providers hand out from task 6 on. Criterion 3.2 is claimed by task 7, where its last sentences become derived. Criterion 6.2 is claimed by task 10, where the last of its classes leaves the product code. Criterion 10.1 is claimed by task 12, and each earlier task still updates the page whose sentence it makes false in its own pull request.

**The diff is run again at task 12**, traced to the tests, files and strings the work produced and not to a task's promise, and two traces are read back to their artefacts to check that the evidence is that criterion's and not a neighbour's.
